memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting. While he watches, the heifer is to be burned — its hide, flesh, blood and intestines. The priest is to take some cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer. — Num 19:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blood is sprinkled seven times toward the tent of meeting, and then the entire heifer is burned — everything, holding nothing back. The number seven in Scripture often signals completeness, and here it speaks of a full and perfect provision. Nothing was left undone; the whole animal was given over for the cleansing of God's people.

There is a solemn truth at the heart of this: cleansing costs a life. The defilement of God's people could not simply be waved away or ignored. Something had to die. The heifer's death provided what the people needed to be made clean. This principle runs all through Scripture — sin and defilement are dealt with not by pretending they do not exist, but by the giving of a life.

The hyssop and scarlet wool mentioned here appear again in other cleansing ceremonies, tools by which the cleansing was applied. God gave His people tangible means to receive what the sacrifice provided. He did not leave them guessing how to be made clean.

All of this points us to the cross, where the true and complete cleansing was accomplished. Just as the heifer was wholly given, Christ gave Himself entirely for us, holding nothing back. And just as hyssop applied the cleansing of old, hyssop appears again at the cross, lifted to Jesus in His thirst. The sevenfold sprinkling of blood finds its fulfilment in His blood, which cleanses completely and forever. We do not need this ceremony repeated, because Christ's one perfect offering has done what all these shadows only pictured.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Why can defilement not simply be ignored or waved away?
2. What does it mean that our cleansing cost the life of Christ?
3. How does the completeness of Jesus' sacrifice reassure you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You did not simply ignore my sin but provided full cleansing at great cost. Thank You that Christ gave Himself completely for me, holding nothing back. I rest in His finished and perfect work. Amen.
